title: Dynamic Distribution of Gallbladder Microbiota in Rabbits at Different Ages and Health States
author: Yawei Xing
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.xarfid6
materials: Microbial genomic DNA was extracted from 1000 mg of each gallbladder sample and 500 mg of each fecal sample. Microbial genomic DNA was extracted from the samples using the QiaAmp DNA Stool Mini Kit (Qiagen, Hilden, Germany) following the manufacturer’s instructions. The quality of DNA was detected by 0.8% agarose gel electrophoresis. The concentration and purity of DNA were examined using spectrophotometry on NanoDrop (Fisher Scientific, Schwerte, Germany). 岛

The V4 hypervariable region of 16S rRNA was amplified by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) using specific barcoded primers (515F: 5’-GTGCCAGCMGCCGCGGTAA-3’ and 806R: 5’-GGACTACHVGGGTWTCTA AT-3’). All PCR procedures were performed using the Phusion High-Fidelity PCR Master Mix (New England Biolabs, Ipswich, MA, USA) with the PCR programs. The PCR was run in a total reaction volume of 25 μL. Each reaction mixture contained 2.5-μL 10×PCR buffer, 2-μL dNTP, 2-μL forward and reverse primers (1 μL each), 0.5-μL Taq DNA polymerase, 2-μL DNA template, and 11-μL sterile water. The PCR conditions were as follows: initial denaturation at 94°C for 5 minutes, followed by 25 cycles of 94°C denaturation for 30 seconds, 50°C of annealing for 30 seconds, 72°C of extension for 30 seconds, and a final extension at 72°C for 7 minutes [26]. A mixture of PCR products was purified using the Qiagen Gel Extraction Kit (Qiagen, Hilden, Germany). Then the PCR products were used to generate a sequencing library with the TruSeq DNA PCRFREE Sample Preparation Kit (Illumina HiSeq 2500 platform, San Diego, CA, USA). Finally, the library was sequenced on the Illumina HiSeq 2500 platform and a 250-bp paired end read was generated. e

steps.title: Select and house rabbits
steps.instruction: Obtain twelve healthy male New Zealand White rabbits (Medical Experimental Animal Center of Hunan Province, China). Use five young rabbits (3 weeks old, pre‑weaning) and seven adult rabbits (18 weeks old) fed regular rabbit chow. Wean rabbits at 4 weeks of age.

steps.title: Euthanize and collect gallbladders
steps.instruction: Euthanize each rabbit by intravenous injection of pentobarbital sodium at 150 mg/kg. Perform the procedure on a super‑clean bench, resect the gallbladder from each animal (total 12 gallbladders), and store the samples at –80 °C until further use.

steps.title: Collect and store fecal samples
steps.instruction: Collect fecal samples from the adult rabbits while they are fasting, place the samples on dry ice or directly into a –80 °C freezer, and store until DNA extraction.

steps.title: Process raw 16S sequencing data
steps.instruction: Use the QIIME pipeline (version 1.9.1) to process raw sequencing reads.

substeps.instruction: Splice and filter raw reads to remove disturbance (dirty) data, producing clean data.
Apply chimera filtration to the clean data to obtain effective data for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Cluster sequences into OTUs
steps.instruction: Cluster the effective tags from all samples into operational taxonomic units (OTUs) at 97 % sequence identity.

substeps.instruction: Select a representative sequence for each OTU.
Classify each representative sequence using the Greengenes database version gg_13_8.

steps.title: Generate relative abundance tables
steps.instruction: For each sample, identify the most abundant taxon at each taxonomic level (phylum, class, order, family, genus) and calculate the relative abundance of all species.

steps.title: Calculate diversity indices
steps.instruction: Compute the Shannon‑Weaver diversity index, ACE, and Chao1 for each sample, taking into account species number and evenness.

steps.title: Perform phylogenetic analysis
steps.instruction: Align sequences and construct a phylogenetic tree using the PyNAST method, then use the tree for Unweighted UniFrac Principal Coordinate Analysis (PCoA).

steps.title: Analyze OTU overlap
steps.instruction: Identify common and unique OTUs among the different groups; if the number of groups is less than five, draw a Venn diagram.

steps.title: Predict microbial functions
steps.instruction: Predict functional profiles of the microbial communities using the FAPROTAX database.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of results
steps.instruction: Express measurement data as mean ± standard deviation. Perform one‑way analysis of variance (ANOVA) using SPSS software version 22.0 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA). Consider differences statistically significant when P < 0.05.
